From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Connor / Karthik — forwarding Marc's ask. Need quick guidance on pricing and the recommended operational path. Key constraints: 6-hour window, 3.5x QPS spike, ClearSail won't take a sustained commit. They asked for predictable cost and minimal invoice surprises.

My suggested matrix (input for your review):
1) Instant Top-up (on-demand short window)
   - Activation: manual by Redwood ops, duration up to 12 hours
   - Billing: 6-hour pro rata of short-window rate = 1.8x standard per-QPS unit (minor surcharge to cover priority capacity)
   - Overrun: immediate overrun billed at 2.5x standard rate if they exceed declared top-up QPS
   - Reconciliation: invoice line-item with start/end timestamps; no post-hoc true-up unless overrun threshold triggered

2) Soft Headroom (capped headroom with soft overrun)
   - Activation: pre-provisioned headroom for the window; can be enabled from console or via API
   - Billing: flat headroom fee = $X/hour (covering reserved ephemeral capacity) + pay-as-you-go token usage at standard rate
   - Overrun: if usage > headroom + declared QPS, overrun billed at 1.5x standard; customer gets 1 free rollback minute for transient spikes
   - Reconciliation: monthly true-up to reconcile headroom fees and actual usage; overrun credited if network/Redwood fault contributed

3) Micro-Commit (short-term prorated commit)
   - Activation: customer signs an amendment (email OK) to commit to a small temporary capacity for 1–7 days
   - Billing: prorated commit price (e.g., 24-hour minimum) with lower unit price (0.85x standard)
   - Overrun: overrun billed at 1.2x standard; any unused commit hours are credited on monthly invoice

Questions for ops:
- Can we guarantee activation lead time of 60 minutes? (we need to confirm scheduling and a playbook)
- Any constraints on rapid scale to 3.5x for a 6-hour window in us-west-2?

If OK, I'll draft a short customer-facing sheet (one page) and attach the pricing matrix.

Thanks — Mina

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Marc — thanks for the details and the load-plan. We ran this by product and ops; below are three concise options so you can decide quickly. I attached a pricing matrix and a short terms summary (see attachments).

Option A — Instant Top-up (fastest)
- Activation: Redwood ops enable capacity within ~60 minutes of PO/approval
- Duration & Cost: pro-rated by hour; estimated cost for your 6-hour window = $2,700 (based on 1.8x short-window unit rate)
- Overrun: billed at 2.5x standard; we will notify at 80% of declared QPS

Option B — Soft Headroom (safer; low friction)
- Activation: pre-provisioned runbook; enable via console/API
- Duration & Cost: headroom fee $300/hour + standard usage; estimated cost = $2,100 plus token usage
- Overrun: 1.5x standard; monthly reconciliation with credits if platform fault

Option C — Micro-Commit (lowest unit rate)
- Activation: sign amendment (email accepted) — 24-hour minimum
- Duration & Cost: prorated commit at 0.85x unit price; estimated cost = $1,900 (includes unused-hour credit if not consumed)
- Overrun: 1.2x standard; billed on monthly invoice

Recommended: If you need the simplest, lowest-risk route with predictable cost, choose Option C (micro-commit) — we can issue an amendment via email now and provision within 60 minutes of your confirmation. If speed is the priority, Option A is the fastest to enable.

Next steps:
- Reply with the option you prefer + a short confirmation line (e.g., "Confirm micro-commit 6h 3.5x")
- I will attach the amendment and the invoice note; operations will schedule the enablement and set up monitoring/alerts for you

Attachments: QS_Pricing_Matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), Transient-Headroom-Terms.pdf (pdf)

Best,
